Q: How can I store a command in a variable in a shell script? A:

I will post an addition to the question so that search engines can provide better results.

Often when using compound commands for bash -c, the following error is thrown:

Error: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching"' `

Examples of error generation

#!/bin/bash


bash -c "ls -l"
# success

command="ls -l"
bash -c "$command"
#success

command="-c \"ls\""
bash $command
#success

command="bash -c \"ls\""
$command
#success

command="-c \"ls \""
bash $command
#error: ": -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `"'

command="-c \"ls -l\""
bash $command
#error:  -l": -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `"'

command="bash -c \"ls \""
$command
#Error: ": -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `"'

command="bash -c 'ls -l'"
$command
#error: -l': -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `''

command='bash -c "echo hello"'
$command
#error: hello": -c: line 1: unexpected EOF while looking for matching `"'

If you dive deeper, the problem of quotes arises in any compound command

#!/bin/bash

docker run --mount type=bind,src="path",dst="path" #...
#success


command='docker run --mount type=bind,src="path",dst="path"'
$command
#Error: invalid argument "type=bind,src=\"path\",dst=\"path\"" for "--mount" flag: parse error on line 1, column 15: bare " in non-quoted-field

Initially, the problem was discovered when creating a script to launch a docker container with parameters

Example

#!/bin/bash

command="$@"
docker run --rm --entrypoint "bash" image -c "$command"
#success

 #In perspective, if there are no arguments, the command variable is completely empty.
command="-c \"$@\"" 
docker run --rm --entrypoint "bash" image $command
#error

Solution options

#We turn the literal representation of a string into code
source <(echo "$command")

as said above - representation of a command through an array

command=( $command )
"${command[@]}"

but this option is not desirable, since the escape quotes remain as letters (they will not be part of the command and will be perceived in the execution line as escape quotes)

Example error:

 command="docker run -it --rm  --mount type=bind,src=\"/dir/path\",dst=\"/dir/path\"  --entrypoint \"bash\"  ubuntu:latest $@"
#or - '
# command='docker run -it --rm  --mount type=bind,src="/dir/path",dst="/dir/path" --entrypoint "bash"  ubuntu:latest $@'
command=( $command )
"${command[@]}"

# Error: invalid argument "type=bind,src=\"/dir/path\",dst=\"/dir/path\"" for "--mount" flag: parse error on line 1, column 15: bare " in non-quoted-field

Q: About Learning Big Data for First Time A:

Don’t jump straight into big data. First learn Excel basics (sorting, formulas, pivot tables), then focus on SQL since you already have MySQL. After that, pick up Python (especially Pandas) for data analysis. Once your fundamentals are strong, big data tools like Hadoop or Spark will make much more sense.

Q: Base + Offset Addressing Mode A:

This is what happens when performing an LDR using a base register R6 and destination register R2:

MAR<-R6 + IR[5:0]
MDR<-MEM[MAR]
R2<-MDR

Let's say R6 = x3000, IR[5:0] = x5, and R2 = 0 (although this value doesn't matter since it will be loaded with another value at the end).

MAR<-R6 + IR[5:0]

R6 is added to IR[5:0] (which is the offset value in the last six bits of the LDR instruction). The base x3000 (value of R6) has x5 (value of IR[5:0]) added to it, giving us x3005. The MAR (memory address register) now holds x3005.

MDR<-MEM[MAR]

The value in the MAR (x3005) is loaded into the MDR (memory data register).

R2<-MDR

The value in the MDR (x3005) is loaded into R2. R2 now holds the value: x3005.

Q: ORA-12533: TNS:illegal ADDRESS parameters A:

SERVER should be DEDICATED or SHARED

DEPL_D.WORLD=
    (DESCRIPTION=
        (ADDRESS_LIST =
            (ADDRESS=
                (PROTOCOL = tcp)
                (HOST = XX.XXX.X.XXX)
                (PORT = XXXX)
            )
        )
        (CONNECT_DATA =
            (SERVICE_NAME = DEPL_D)
            (SERVER = DEDICATED)
        )
   )

or

DEPL_D.WORLD=
    (DESCRIPTION=
        (ADDRESS_LIST =
            (ADDRESS=
                (PROTOCOL = tcp)
                (HOST = XX.XXX.X.XXX)
                (PORT = XXXX)
            )
        )
        (CONNECT_DATA =
            (SERVICE_NAME = DEPL_D)
        )
   )
